title: Event Modifiers: Making Events Smarter
description: Simplify common event tasks with built-in modifiers like .stop, .prevent, and .once.

slides.title: What are Modifiers?
slides.content:
# Modifiers: Tiny Helpers Event modifiers are special suffixes you add to `v-on` to handle common event‑related tasks without writing extra JavaScript. ```html
...
...
``` They make your templates cleaner and your code more declarative.

slides.title: Common Modifiers
slides.content:
| Modifier | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `.stop` | Calls `event.stopPropagation()` |
| `.prevent` | Calls `event.preventDefault()` |
| `.once` | Trigger the handler only once |
| `.self` | Trigger only if `event.target` is the element itself |
| `.capture` | Use capture mode when adding the event listener |
| `.passive` | Indicates the handler will never call `preventDefault()` (improves scroll performance) |

You can chain modifiers: `@click.stop.prevent="onClick"`.

quizData.question: Which modifier would you use to prevent the default browser action (e.g., form submission)?
quizData.explanation: `.prevent` calls `event.preventDefault()`, which stops the default browser behavior.
